title: Build apartments and commercial buildings to the building code (NCC Volume One)
what: Comply with the Building Rules, which include the Building Code of Australia (NCC Volume One, with the South Australian variations), in performing building work on Class 2 to 9 buildings. The edition in force is NCC 2022 until the building code moves to NCC 2025 on 1 May 2027 (the plumbing code moved on 1 May 2026). Its schedule in NCC 2025 varies 82 national provisions, mostly special use buildings and ancillary provisions.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset. Quoted from the corpus copy of the official text (SA register as at 2024).

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume One) as South Australia applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
